# Lane OS

> A home repo for Claude Code that runs many windows at once: parallel, single-topic "lanes" over a shared, persistent context spine, each window locked to its own lane by a hook, with only the home window rebuilding the shared state. Lane OS is a repository layout plus a small set of hooks, checks, skills and conventions. It is a scaffold, not a dependency: you clone it, make it yours, and the conventions and the checks do the work.

Lane OS solves three problems: (1) parallel sessions conflict when they all write the same shared state, (2) every new session starts amnesiac, and (3) rules held only in prose decay. The fixes: "one window = one topic" enforced by the write-lane invariant (a session may write only the lane it owns); a synthesis layer (brain/, memory/) read on demand via a pointer hook; rules that load only where they apply, one line each pointing to a memory file; and gates kept for harm that is outward or cannot be undone. A correction is a note first, becomes a rule on the second miss and gets a hook only when the harm is outward.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what Lane OS is, what you get (ordered by what is hardest to find elsewhere), the layout, quickstart, and what it does not do.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): adopt it step by step.
- [Philosophy](docs/philosophy.md): one window = one topic, and why.

## Core concepts

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): the three lane types and the shared spine.
- [The write-lane invariant](docs/write-lane-invariant.md): the safety rule that makes parallelism work, the guard, and the test that proves the guard blocks.
- [Session lifecycle](docs/session-lifecycle.md): the SessionStart pointer hook, restart versus refresh.
- [Gated rules](docs/gated-rules.md): gated or judgment, when a gate earns its place, the retired coverage ratchet, why a fail-open guard needs a self-test.
- [The miss-to-rule loop](docs/miss-to-rule-loop.md): a note first, a rule on the second miss, a gate only where it earns its place; where each rule's line loads.
- [Concerns](docs/concerns.md): every open concern declares a Probe or an Owner.
- [Context budgets](docs/context-budgets.md): byte budgets on every file a session reads whole, one table.
- [Behavioural rules](docs/agent-toward-human.md): how the agent treats the human; the reply envelope.
- [Memory](docs/memory.md): durable facts, one file per fact, frontmatter-indexed.
- [The voice layer](docs/voice-layer.md): distilled rules plus a raw corpus, one register per lane, and the thirteen-check linter that reads a draft before a human does.

## Operating it

- [Drift checks](docs/drift-checks.md): audit-cheap's sixteen checks and the staged commit gate.
- [The reply-length gate](docs/reply-length-gate.md): a Stop hook that measures, a UserPromptSubmit hook that instructs.
- [The switchboard](docs/switchboard.md): what the other windows are doing, and what each lane is on.
- [Rules sync and shared repos](docs/rules-sync-and-shared-repos.md): propagation that defers around live sessions and never reaches a repo an outside reader sees; the publisher.
- [Parallel lanes and worktrees](docs/parallel-lanes-worktrees.md): two sessions in one lane.
- [Multi-machine](docs/multi-machine.md): symlinks, sync, working across machines.
- [Code from anywhere](docs/code-from-anywhere.md): real, non-sandbox sessions from your phone.
- [Skills](skills): catchup, since, spark, spin-lane, recall, reflect, preflight, ship.

## Key files

- [global/CLAUDE.md](global/CLAUDE.md): the rules for every session, one line each, each naming its memory file.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the rules for sessions inside the spine.
- [memory/](memory): one fact per file; the rule files the loaded lines name.
- [global/REFERENCE.md](global/REFERENCE.md): hooks, checks, scripts, environment variables, routing.
- [hooks/session-start.sh](hooks/session-start.sh): detects the lane, pulls the spine, prints the lane rules and the read-directive.
- [scripts/hooks/block-cross-lane-write.py](scripts/hooks/block-cross-lane-write.py): the PreToolUse guard that enforces the invariant.
- [scripts/audit-cheap.sh](scripts/audit-cheap.sh): the drift checks.
- [scripts/check-voice.py](scripts/check-voice.py): the voice linter; `--list`, `--self-test`, `--measure`.
- [scripts/probe-concerns.py](scripts/probe-concerns.py), [scripts/check-file-budgets.py](scripts/check-file-budgets.py), [scripts/sync-rules.py](scripts/sync-rules.py), [scripts/publish-shared-repo.py](scripts/publish-shared-repo.py), [scripts/build-switchboard.py](scripts/build-switchboard.py).

## Optional

- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): the whole documentation set concatenated into one fetchable file.
